newsitem.title: USA: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-HOLTZ QUITS NOTRE DAME.
newsitem.headline: AMERICAN FOOTBALL-HOLTZ QUITS NOTRE DAME.

text.p: Lou Holtz announced his resignation Tuesday from the most prestigious job in college football, stepping down as coach at Notre Dame, effective at the end of the season.
While ending a week of speculation, Holtz would not reveal why he is leaving South Bend, nor would he discuss his future plans.

"I cannot honestly give you a reason for my resignation, except to say I feel it is the right thing to do," Holtz said in a prepared statement. "People will say there has to be more to it than this, but believe me, there isn't."
No replacement was named, but Northwestern coach Gary Barnett said today he has been contacted by Notre Dame officials.

Holtz has a record of 99-29-2 at Notre Dame and is second to Knute Rockne on the school's all-time victory list. The 59-year-old Holtz has said he would rather not break Rockne's record of 105 victories.
Notre Dame currently is 7-2 and ranked 10th in the nation.

"I have absolutely no plans for the future. My health (to my knowledge) is good, and I feel as much enthusiasm for life as I did when I became head coach at the age of 32," said Holtz, who miss several games in 1995 after undergoing neck surgery.
Holtz coached the New York Jets in 1976, but was just 3-10 and resigned with one game left in the season.
Holtz was also coach at William & Mary, North Carolina State, Arkansas and Minnesota and has a lifetime collegiate record of 215-94-7.
